items.description: Sec. 4.1 says only that the network and SIMP runs share 'the same cantilever beam boundary condition'. The text never says which region is fixed, how much of it, or which degrees of freedom. These are shown only in Fig. 3(a), which is not available. 'Cantilever' suggests one fully clamped end, but the size of the clamped region is not given.
readings: Entire end face x = 0 (the 20x8-element face, all 21x9 nodes) clamped in ux, uy and uz (Liu-Tovar default cantilever)
Only a central patch of the x = 0 face clamped
Only the top and bottom edge lines of the x = 0 face clamped

items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives no load location; it appears only in Fig. 3(a). A cantilever suggests a load at the free end, but where on the end face (bottom, middle or top) is not stated.
readings: Free end x = L, bottom edge y = 0 (Liu-Tovar default)
Free end x = L, mid-height y = 0.5H
Free end x = L, top edge y = H

items.description: The text does not say whether the load is a point load, a line load across the 8-element depth, or a pressure over a face. This is shown only in Fig. 3(a).
readings: Line load across the full depth z = 0..D: equal forces on all 9 nodes of the edge (Liu-Tovar default)
Single point load at the mid-depth node (z = 0.5D)
Uniform pressure over the whole free-end face

items.description: The load direction is not stated in the text, only in Fig. 3(a). Because the 40x20x8 dimensions are not tied to axes, it is unclear whether the beam bends across the 20-element side or the 8-element side. The sign of the load does not matter, since compliance is quadratic in the load.
readings: Transverse, parallel to the 20-element side (-y if nely = 20): bending in the 40x20 plane
Transverse, parallel to the 8-element side: bending through the thin dimension

items.description: No load magnitude is given anywhere. The loss (Eq. 20) uses c/c0, so the optimization itself does not depend on it. However, the reported compliances c = 40.6 (network) and c = 37.8 (SIMP) in Fig. 3 do.
readings: Unit force (-1) at each loaded node (Liu-Tovar default; total 9 for a 9-node line)
Total force of 1 split equally among the loaded nodes
A physical force value (e.g. 1 kN)

items.description: Eq. (20) and Sec. 3.5 use V*, but the paper gives no numeric value for Sec. 4.1 or Fig. 3 (or anywhere else).
readings: 0.3 (Liu-Tovar example default)

items.entity: density/sensitivity filter in the SIMP baseline (Fig. 3(c))
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says the network avoids checkerboard patterns 'without needing filtering'. It does not say whether the SIMP baseline (c = 37.8) used a filter or what radius. That baseline was built in the same machine-learning framework on the Liu-Tovar code, which normally includes a density filter.
readings: No filter (raw element densities)
Density filter, radius 1.5 elements (Liu-Tovar default)
Sensitivity filter, radius 1.5 elements
Density filter with a larger radius (2-3 elements)

items.entity: topology network (Eq. 1): number, grid and scale of the Fourier-feature kernels
items.description: Sec. 3.1 says kernels are 'initialized in a linear 3D grid' using TensorFlow's RandomFourierFeatures. It gives no kernel count, grid size, kernel scale or initialization for the output layer. These set the smallest feature size and smoothness of the network result in Fig. 3(b), which acts like an implicit filter.
readings: One kernel per element on a 40x20x8 grid (6400 features)
Coarser kernel grid, e.g. 20x10x4 (800 features)
TensorFlow's default kernel scale with a fixed feature count (e.g. 1000)

items.entity: optimizer settings (SGD for iterations 1-100, Adam for 101-300)
items.description: Sec. 4.1 names the optimizers and the 300 iterations but gives no learning rates, momentum or Adam beta values. A standard topology-optimization solver would use OC or MMA instead. These choices affect the oscillation seen in Fig. 3(d) and which local optimum is reached.
readings: TensorFlow defaults: SGD learning rate 0.01 with no momentum; Adam learning rate 0.001, betas (0.9, 0.999)
Larger rates, e.g. SGD 0.1 and Adam 0.01
Standard OC (move limit 0.2) or MMA updates for 300 iterations

items.entity: schedule for the volume-penalty weight alpha1 (Eq. 20)
items.description: Sec. 3.5 says alpha1 starts at 0 and is 'gradually' increased every iteration up to 100. The step size is not given, so it is unknown how closely the volume target is met by iteration 300.
readings: Linear ramp from 0 to 100 over the 300 iterations
Fixed step per iteration capped at 100 (e.g. +1 per iteration, reaching the cap at iteration 100)
Replace the penalty with a hard volume constraint (OC bisection or MMA)

items.entity: initial design and density bounds (SIMP baseline variables and network weights)
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says the SIMP baseline is a one-layer network with constant input 1 and one output per element. It does not say how outputs are kept between 0 and 1 (sigmoid or clipping) or what the starting values are. The network's starting weights are not given either; the paper only says c0 is computed for a uniform field at V*.
readings: Uniform density = V* in every element, values clipped to [0, 1]
Variables passed through a sigmoid and started at the value that gives V*
Random network weights (non-uniform starting field)

items.entity: axis assignment of the 40x20x8 element grid
items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives '40x20x8 elements' without saying which axis each number belongs to; the coordinate system is defined only in Fig. 2(a). Sec. 4.2 says the higher-resolution version of the same problem (4 batches of 5400 voxels, 21600 in total, about 60x30x12) is split 'evenly in the y-direction'. That split works with whole element layers only if y is the 12- or 60-element direction. So the usual mapping (40 along x, 20 along y, 8 along z) is not certain.
readings: x = 40 (span), y = 20 (height, load direction), z = 8 (depth)
x = 40 (span), y = 8 (height, load direction), z = 20 (width)

items.entity: element edge length / physical domain size
items.description: No physical dimensions or element size are given. The solver based on the Liu-Tovar code normally uses unit cubes, while the network's input coordinates are scaled to [-0.5, 0.5] along the longest edge (Sec. 3.4). This changes the absolute compliance values but not the layout.
readings: Unit cubic elements: domain 40 x 20 x 8
Longest edge scaled to 1: domain 1 x 0.5 x 0.2, element size 0.025
